name: model-scan
title: Model Scan
description: A photo becoming a 3D character, driven by an engine's events through props: landmark groups light up over the photo, the photo burns into particles while the camera turns to a three-quarter view and the base model appears where it stood, streamed weights reshape it, the final character fades in over it, and it hands over to orbit. Reduced motion crossfades instead. Announces each stage; agents get cancel and retry.
docs: `<ModelScan src alt width height stage points model weights targetNames expressions progress statusText error onCancel onRetry modelAlt idleClip aspectRatio fit viewer actions labels>`: `stage` is `photo`, `detecting`, `building`, `refining`, `ready` or `error`: the UI's, which you map from your engine's. `points` light up while detecting: one list (a Float32Array of interleaved x, y fractions of the original photo, or `{ x, y }` objects), or groups `{ source, points, aspect? }` (the face, the body) that each light up on their own, in the order their sources arrived, a later group replacing its source's. They land straight on the photo where the stage draws it, following `fit` (`contain`, or `cover` in a stage of another `aspectRatio`); points past 0 or 1, landmarks a crop cut off, are kept but not drawn and don't count in the stagger. `aspect` is the photo's own width over height: until the photo loads, it sizes the stage when `width` and `height` aren't given. `error` is the line a person reads at `error`: map your engine's error codes to your own words (ModelScan knows none), and leave `onRetry` out when a new run can't help, like a browser without WebGL2. `model` is the base GLB with morph targets, from `building` on: a URL, its bytes, or `{ glb, targetNames }` as an engine sends it; pass the final character the same way when it arrives and it fades in over the base model keeping the weights (at once when they look the same). `weights` are its morph weights, a Float32Array aligned with the target names or a map by name, eased as they stream; `expressions` by ARKit name, like a smile at the end. `progress` is 0 to 1 within the stage, on the progress bar under the stage (indeterminate without it). At `building` the photo moves into the 3D scene on a plane the front camera sees exactly where the 2D photo was, so nothing jumps; the camera then eases to the three-quarter view while the photo burns away into particles and the model fades in, all on the GPU. Under reduced motion the photo crossfades into the model, with no camera flight or particles, and the camera jumps after. At `ready` the idle clip plays (`idleClip`, or the model's first) unless motion is reduced, and the viewer's controls appear. It builds on ModelViewer (pass more of its props through `viewer`), whose scene chunk starts loading at `detecting`; the transition is a second small chunk. Screen readers hear each stage (`labels.stage`), progress at most every tenth and two seconds, and the error at once. Cancel shows before `ready` when `onCancel` is set, Retry at `error` with `onRetry`, beside your `actions`; when the control that had focus there goes with the stage (a start button as the run begins, Cancel as it ends), focus moves to the first enabled one. Agents call `cancel` and `retry`, and a call outside its stage throws with the reason.
